title: Time travel: closed timelike curves
example_questions: What if we could travel back in time?
Could a wormhole be a time machine?
summary: Some solutions of general relativity contain closed timelike curves, paths through spacetime that return to their own past, such as Godel's rotating universe or a wormhole whose mouths age differently. Hawking's chronology protection conjecture proposes that quantum effects always prevent such time machines from forming.
support_note: Allowed mathematically; most physicists expect nature to forbid them.
what_happens: One wormhole mouth is moved at high speed so it ages less
The mouths become offset in time
Quantum fluctuations may build up and destroy the wormhole before a loop forms

sources.title: An example of a new type of cosmological solutions of Einstein's field equations of gravitation
Wormholes, time machines, and the weak energy condition
sources.authors: M. S. Morris, K. S. Thorne, U. Yurtsever
